Adds a 64-bit RISC-V port for the [orbit-rv](https://github.com/coopersimpson101-debug/orbit-rv) CPU and QEMU, and fixes two latent memory-management bugs found by [proofstack](https://github.com/coopersimpson101-debug/proofstack).

## Highlights
- `rv64` board (RV64IMA_Zicsr_Zifencei): M-mode entry with PMP and a built-in SBI shim, S-mode traps, Sv39 paging with W^X kernel sections, SBI timer preemption, PLIC + NS16550 console, U-mode tasks. Fits in the 256 KiB of RAM on the orbit-rv FPGA SoC
- Boots in QEMU riscv64 `virt` in CI, on the orbit-rv golden ISS, and on the orbit-rv RTL in simulation (all 5,978,340 commits match the ISS)
- AArch64 code factored behind `arch.h` / `context.h` / `hal.h`, so both ports share the scheduler, allocator, drivers and shell
- Fixed: `buddy_add_range` with a range overlapping managed pages handed a page out twice; AArch64 `map_range` dropped the last page of an unaligned range. Neither path is reached by today's boot code. Both now have regression tests, and proofstack proves the fixed allocator's invariant in Lean for every range

## Downloads
- `orbit-os-rv64.elf` and `orbit-os-rv64.bin`: RISC-V image for QEMU `virt` (`-bios none`) and orbit-rv
- `orbit-os-rpi5.zip`: SD-card bundle (kernel_2712.img, kernel8.img, chainloader.img, config.txt)
- `orbit-os-rpi5.elf` and `orbit-os-qemu-virt.elf`

## Not yet verified
These need real hardware and are tracked in the README's Status table:
- First boot on real Pi 5 hardware (UART and GIC addresses still to confirm)
- Boot on orbit-rv running on a real ULX3S FPGA board
